headline: South Asia: Makkah defence pact meeting to be held today in Riyadh, confirms FO
script:
Good afternoon. This is your global conflict briefing.

BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT:
- South Asia: Makkah defence pact meeting to be held today in Riyadh, confirms FO.
- Western Russia: Three killed and 39 injured, including children, in at least three Russian guided bomb strikes on Kharkiv – video, photos.
- Africa: Sudan: Sudan Doctors Network - Four Civilians Killed in RSF Drone Attacks On South Kordofan.

Full breakdown follows.

NORTH AMERICA
United States - bottom line: Aboard the USS George Washington, young sailors adjust to war with Iran.
- Military Times, 2 hours ago: Aboard the USS George Washington, young sailors adjust to war with Iran.
Sailors must maintain a ​state of alert and readiness, heightened in the case of the George Washington due to the threat of Iranian attacks.
- Military Times, 2 hours ago: US Army tests counter-drone tech at Mexican border as cartel drone use rises.
The service is seeking to sharpen its defenses against the growing threat of drone use by cartels.
The Caribbean - bottom line: ‘UNINFORMED’ - Global Afrikan Congress rebukes Warmington over slave trade remarks, urges him to do research and apologise.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 12 hours ago: ‘UNINFORMED’ - Global Afrikan Congress rebukes Warmington over slave trade remarks, urges him to do research and apologise.
The Global Afrikan Congress (GAC) is demanding an apology from parliamentarian Everald Warmington for his “uninformed assertions” that Black Africans who sold people into the transatlantic slave trade should be held more accountable than Europeans buyers. In an open letter to Warmington, the GAC – an international Pan-African organisation of people of African descent across 35 countries – also urged the St Catherine South Western member of parliament (MP) to undertake necessary research to correct his “colonial miseducation”.
Central America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

SOUTH AMERICA
South America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

EUROPE
Western Russia - bottom line: Three killed and 39 injured, including children, in at least three Russian guided bomb strikes on Kharkiv – video, photos.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 5 hours ago: Three killed and 39 injured, including children, in at least three Russian guided bomb strikes on Kharkiv – video, photos.
Russian forces attacked the city of Kharkiv with at least three guided aerial bombs and a combat drone on 5 October, killing three people and leaving 35 others in need of medical treatment, including children.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 3 hours ago: One dead and three injured in three Russian airstrikes on Sloviansk.
A woman was killed and three other people, including a 13-year-old boy, were injured as a result of three Russian airstrikes on the Sloviansk hromada in Donetsk Oblast on 5 October.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 5 hours ago: Officers involved in strikes on Ukraine were among eight killed in Tu-95MS crash in Russia.
Eight military personnel, including at least three officers linked to combat missions or their preparation by the Ukrainian project Book of Executioners, were killed when a Russian Tu-95MS strategic bomber crashed in Amur Oblast on 29 September.
- Ukrainska Pravda, Times of India - Top Stories, 2 hours ago: Russian drones attack Turkish vessel, captain killed – Zelenskyy.
Zelenskyy says two Russian drones hit a Turkish-owned civilian vessel carrying maize in neutral waters, killing its captain.
Southern Europe - bottom line: Kosovo Parliament Moves Towards Changing Law to Curb Hague Special Court.
- Balkan Insight, 4 hours ago: Kosovo Parliament Moves Towards Changing Law to Curb Hague Special Court.
MPs in first reading adopt major changes to law governing the Hague-based war crimes court following conviction of former Kosovo Liberation Army leaders – although enforcement requires second vote.
- Politico Europe, 6 hours ago: Suspected plague in Russia puts EU on alert.
“We are aware of the reports concerning the laboratory incident in Russia, seemingly involving a pathogen-causing plague,” says European Commission spokesperson.
- Politico Europe, 10 hours ago: Is Kemi Badenoch abandoning the Red Wall?.
Is Andy Burnham an easier opponent for the Conservatives than Sir Keir Starmer? At the Tory conference in Birmingham, Kemi Badenoch’s team sniff a chance to attack the prime minister – with a particular chance to seize on and attack his economic argument. Sam Coates and Anne McElvoy pore over Badenoch’s “The Right Way” pamphlet […]
- Balkan Insight, 11 hours ago: Hungary’s New Government Haunted by Orban’s House of Terror.
The fate of Budapest’s House of Terror, a controversial museum which focuses on life under totalitarianism in the 20th century, could spark another round of the ‘culture war’.

AFRICA
Africa - bottom line: Sudan: Sudan Doctors Network - Four Civilians Killed in RSF Drone Attacks On South Kordofan.
- AllAfrica - Conflict, 7 hours ago: Sudan: Sudan Doctors Network - Four Civilians Killed in RSF Drone Attacks On South Kordofan.
[Dabanga] Dilling, South Kordofan -- Four civilians, including a child and a woman, have been killed in RSF drone strikes on residential neighbourhoods in Dilling, South Kordofan, the Sudan Doctors Network says. The network condemns the attacks as a grave violation of international humanitarian law.
- AllAfrica - Conflict, 12 hours ago: Sudan: Sudan War - Fighting On Ethiopian Border, Drone Attacks On Ed Damazin.
[Dabanga] Ed Damazin -- The RSF-aligned Tasees Alliance forces announced on Saturday that they had taken full control of areas in Roseires locality, north-east of Ed Damazin, capital of Sudan's Blue Nile state, after seizing several areas, including Menze, Jabal El Nimr, Jabal El Num, Basharkat, Matanguya, Mangaling El Jawani, Masnabiga, and Makala.
- AllAfrica - Conflict, 12 hours ago: Ethiopia: Ethiopia's New Rebel War Redraws Alliances Across the Horn of Africa.
[RFI] Ethiopia and Eritrea have cut diplomatic ties as a new rebel offensive grips northern Ethiopia, putting two countries that fought together during the last Tigray war on opposing sides. Ethiopia accuses its neighbour of supporting a new anti-government alliance.
- AllAfrica - Conflict, 7 hours ago: Nigeria: 28 Killed Despite Curfew in Plateau.
[Daily Trust] At least 28 people have been killed in a renewed wave of attacks across three local government areas of Plateau State despite a dusk-to-dawn curfew imposed by the state government on September 21 to restore peace and prevent further loss of life.
Persian Gulf Region - bottom line: IDF killed two-thirds of terrorists who invaded Israel on October 7, intel chief tells cabinet.
- Jerusalem Post, 5 hours ago: IDF killed two-thirds of terrorists who invaded Israel on October 7, intel chief tells cabinet.
"There are 2,000 remaining, and we will get to every last one of them," Maj.-Gen. Shlomi Binder, head of the IDF's Military Intelligence, told the security cabinet on Sunday evening.
- Jerusalem Post, just now: Iran plans to expand missile range to reach ‘enemy located at greater distance’, spokesperson says.
The IRGC spokesperson shared that “during this war, we reached the conclusion that we definitely need to increase the range of our missiles, and we have now moved in this direction.”
- Al Jazeera - Middle East, 3 hours ago: US pulls bombers from UK base: Is Iran manoeuvring Trump’s war plans?.
The withdrawal means the US lost a convenient launchpad, not its underlying strike capability, said an expert.
- Jerusalem Post, 3 hours ago: New Zealand police probes flydubai hijacker's time spent in island country - report.
Additionally, the New Zealand Herald reported that Captain Smit Machchhar, the Indian pilot whom Hammami attacked aboard the flydubai flight, had trained in the island country.
South Africa: no notable developments in the last 24 hours.

ASIA
South Asia - bottom line: Makkah defence pact meeting to be held today in Riyadh, confirms FO.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 5 hours ago: Makkah defence pact meeting to be held today in Riyadh, confirms FO.
A meeting of the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement will be held on Monday in Riyadh and will focus on regional developments and ongoing cooperation among the member states, the Foreign Office (FO) confirmed. In a statement on social media platform X, the FO said Pakistan’s delegation to the meeting of the Strategic Political and Defence Committee (SPDC) will include Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar, Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir, and Defence Minister Khawaja Asif.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 2 hours ago: At Moscow moot, Pakistan says terrorism remains core of Afghanistan's problems.
Pakistan’s Special Representative for Afghanistan Mohammad Sadiq on Monday said that terrorism remained at the core of Afghanistan’s problems, reaffirming that Pakistan would continue to take “all appropriate measures” for ensuring the safety of its citizens, in accordance with international law. Sadiq made these remarks at the eighth meeting of Moscow Format Consultations on Afghanistan in the Russian capital.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 14 hours ago: Only ‘just, fair’ talks can end war, Iran tells US.
TEHRAN: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi declared on Sunday that there was no military solution to the US’ war against the Islamic Republic and that only negotiations based on “justice and fairness” could end the conflict, as talks between Washington and Tehran appeared to be at an impasse. “If our enemies again choose the path of military confrontation, our response will be stronger than before, and we will defend ourselves with even more force,” Araghchi told a gathering of foreign ambassadors in Tehran.
- Dawn (Pakistan), just now: ‘Abandoned province’: Amir Muqam slams PTI, says not in favour of governor’s rule in KP but security risks persist.
Minister for Kashmir Affairs and Gilgit-Baltistan Amir Muqam on Monday slammed the PTI-led government in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, stressing that the federal government was not “in favour of governor’s rule” amid the party’s march, but warning of national security risks. The minister’s comments came as KP Chief Minister Sohail Afridi launched the party’s long march towards Islamabad on Sunday, saying that the party would “not accept” any policy against the interests of the people of KP. PTI went ahead with its march despite warnings from the federal government.
India - bottom line: Saudi-led coalition targets Red Sea territory held by Houthis. What's Pak's role?.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 4 hours ago: Saudi-led coalition targets Red Sea territory held by Houthis. What's Pak's role?.
Islamabad has not publicly acknowledged direct involvement in Saudi Arabia's offensive inside Yemen. However, several reports point that Pakistani forces could be helping Saudi Arabia shift more of its military resources towards the war by taking over defensive responsibilities inside the kingdom. That could allow Saudi forces to concentrate on the offensive against the Houthis without Pakistan formally becoming a combatant in Yemen.
- NDTV - Top Stories, South China Morning Post - China, 2 hours ago: 'Intend To Complete Missions': Netanyahu Vows No Hamas Rule In Gaza.
Since Hamas's October 2023 attack, Israel has fought wars on several fronts, including against Iran-backed Hezbollah in Lebanon.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 5 hours ago: Why did AJ Styles return to the ring 246 days after WWE retirement?.
AJ Styles made a surprising return to the wrestling ring to assist his son, Avery, during a match. Avery was attacked by allies of his opponent, Tristan Moody, after winning by disqualification. Styles, who had recently retired, rushed in to help Avery and fought off the attackers. The emotional moment between father and son highlighted the bond they share as wrestling becomes a family affair.
- NDTV - Top Stories, one hour ago: Opposition Plan To Seek Gyanesh Kumar's Sacking Begins Tomorrow With Big March.
Sources said MPs from the INDIA alliance will gather at the Makar Dwar of Parliament on Tuesday and march from there to Nirvachan Sadan -- the Election Commission headquarters.

- South China Morning Post - China, NK News, 7 hours ago: Seoul probe reveals border mine blast caused by North Korea.
South Korea ⁠said on Monday that a ⁠recent border blast that seriously wounded two ⁠of its soldiers was caused by mines planted by North Korea. North Korea, which has been fortifying its border with South Korea since April 2024, deployed up to 7,000 workers to install mines and fences this year, with some 50 incidents of ‌crossing the border, according to a briefing on Monday by the South’s military. Built to hunt tanks and support ground troops, the People’s Liberation Army’s main attack helicopter is increasingly being prepared for operations at sea. Crews of the Z-10 are training to fly from ships – a shift that could give Beijing extra firepower in an amphibious assault on Taiwan. Manufactured by AVIC subsidiary the Changhe Aircraft Industries Corporation, the Z-10 entered service with the PLA Army in late 2010. India is taking a more direct role in efforts to end the conflict between Russia and Ukraine, engaging both sides on issues including shipping and reducing hostilities, Minister of External Affairs S. Jaishankar has said. Speaking at a security conference over the weekend, Jaishankar said India in recent months has become “a little bit more involved beyond advocacy”. - ABC News Australia, Politico Europe, 2 hours ago: Germany at risk of 'violent conflict' with Russia, intelligence chief warns.
